evidence.testTitle: [ADMIN-004 ADMIN-007 ADMIN-008 ADMIN-022 ADMIN-025 ADMIN-026] admin account changes and role revocation enforce independent actor authority
evidence.scenarioScope: Account reenable after actual disable, with independent role and channel controls.
evidence.rationale: Real bootstrap administrator, independently authenticated actors and live IRC/event observers against frozen Worker SQLite.
assertionDetails: Real founder, active IRC operator, ordinary, revoked and anonymous actors cannot grant/revoke Bob admin or enable a disabled account on either alias; four IRC and event observers have a message barrier around denials.
Administrator grants and revokes Bob oper via both aliases; Bob uses OPER on the already connected socket, then revocation emits -o and the same socket is denied OPER and SAJOIN.

Target disable and reenable use both aliases, old session remains invalid, and fresh login succeeds; exact Bob, ircop, Charlie roles and target enabled state are inspected in SQLite and rechecked after recreation.

After recreation an administrator again grants/removes oper and reenables target, while fresh founder and ircop denials and unrelated Charlie bot role survive; no general network-role propagation contract is claimed.

Freshly authenticated root, founder, Bob and Charlie IRC/event witnesses have independent positive message barriers around the post-recreation founder/operator denial block; every observed frame is the barrier.

Before and after each denial block, independent read-only SQLite snapshots compare normalized users, role and nickname rows, user metadata and credential digests plus the founder-channel configuration and grants; session rows and account timestamps are excluded.

evidence.testTitle: [ADMIN-009 ADMIN-010 ADMIN-011 ADMIN-017 ADMIN-025 ADMIN-026] admin aliases configure distinct channels while ordinary founders and IRC operators are denied
evidence.scenarioScope: Administrative channel registration and selected post-recreation controls.
evidence.rationale: Real bootstrap administrator, independently authenticated actors and live IRC/event observers against frozen Worker SQLite.
assertionDetails: Administrator registers two channels via separate aliases with real account founders, reads channel configuration and updates description and F bot welcome through both aliases; authorized topic update is seen on a live member IRC socket.

Founder, active IRC operator, ordinary, revoked and anonymous requests to register, inspect, change info and bot configuration are denied; IRC and event recipient windows have live message barriers and no unauthorized mutation output.

Per-channel SQLite metadata and description prove exact two managed founders, topic, bot setting and independent sentinel; recreation preserves admin reads and unauthorized founder/operator denials, then a fresh admin registration and bot change succeed.
The test observes denial silence and the positive topic IRC event; it does not assert a distinct positive event contract for bot settings or registration.
Fresh root, founder, Bob and Charlie IRC/event witnesses bound the post-recreation registration, bot and info denials with live barriers; every observed frame is the barrier.

Before and after both denial blocks, normalized account state and exact managed-one, managed-two and unrelated channel metadata, permissions, custom roles and assignments are equal; original target and sentinel role IDs and assignee IDs are checked after recreation.
After post-recreation authorized bot update, an independent admin GET reads enabled=true and the exact new welcome value; no unobserved positive bot event is claimed.
